decision_points.question: how is the continuous skin-tone rating turned into the exposure variable, and where (if at all) is it dichotomized?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a rival way to operationalize the primary exposure — a fixed 0.5 split, a 0.25/0.75 split dropping the middle, a data-driven cutoff search, extreme-group cutoffs, or keeping it continuous/standardized; an analyst features one representation, so 41 and 43 co-occurring only 4 times reflects primary-plus-robustness recording, not genuine coexistence

decision_points.question: which regression model is fit to relate exposure to red cards?
decision_points.why_rival: Poisson vs OLS linear-probability are rival choices of the primary regression specification (against the logistic default), and an analysis features one

decision_points.question: which effect-size measure is used to express the exposure's effect on red cards?
decision_points.why_rival: these are alternative expressions of the same effect — odds ratio, risk difference/average marginal effect, relative risk, percentage points, Cohen's h — from which one is designated primary; the heavy 16↔39/32/33 co-occurrence is the same slot recorded twice (a primary measure reported alongside a secondary one), which the guidance flags as expected for genuine rivals

decision_points.question: how are standard errors, confidence intervals, and p-values computed?
decision_points.why_rival: Wald/normal-approximation, analytic delta-method, bootstrap-percentile, and bootstrap-SE-then-Wald are rival methods for quantifying uncertainty; an analyst commits to one for the primary estimate

decision_points.question: along which dimension(s) are the standard errors clustered?
decision_points.why_rival: two-way clustered covariance vs one-way-per-dimension are rival clustering structures for the SEs — a choice separate from the Wald-vs-bootstrap method itself

decision_points.question: by what rule is the hypothesis judged supported?
decision_points.why_rival: these are rival decision rules translating the statistics into a verdict — bare p<0.05, p<0.05 plus a CI excluding the null, or three-/four-way categorical schemes; an analyst applies one, and 42 and 44 never co-occur

decision_points.question: how is the reported evidence selected and framed in the write-up?
decision_points.why_rival: selective supporting bullet points vs curating a chosen subset of estimates (excluding the continuous-exposure result) are rival ways of deciding what evidence to foreground

decision_points.question: how are records with missing values handled?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the disposition of incomplete records (here, listwise deletion to complete cases)

decision_points.question: what prior is placed on the model parameters?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the prior specification for a Bayesian fit (Normal(0,10) on the intercept)

decision_points.question: how is model adequacy or fit assessed?
decision_points.why_rival: in-sample AUC (discrimination) vs Durbin-Watson/residual diagnostics are rival diagnostics tied to the chosen model family for checking fit

decision_points.question: is a power / minimum-detectable-effect analysis computed?
decision_points.why_rival: settles whether and how design sensitivity is quantified (MDE at 80% power)

decision_points.question: how are the results and their uncertainty visualized?
decision_points.why_rival: an odds-ratio forest-style comparison plot vs error bars on raw proportions are rival primary visualizations of the results

decision_points.question: how is statistical significance quantified and reported for the key coefficient?
decision_points.why_rival: which coefficient's Wald p-value is taken as the significance measure, whether p-values are bucketed into significance stars, and whether a one-sided directional test is used are rival conventions for stating significance
